headline: Linux kernel KEV deadline is today and GitLab/Cisco ASA due tomorrow; Palo Alto PHP2Shell chain and Claude Code extension backdoor remain active

bullets.text: Exploited now: GitLab CE/EE CVE-2026-97229 and Cisco ASA/FTD CVE-2026-76418 are in CISA KEV with a 2026-11-01 due date; the Linux kernel flaw CVE-2026-46300 is due today, 2026-10-31.
Palo Alto Networks firewalls are being compromised in chained attacks using PHP2Shell; Help Net Security ties the activity to Chinese hackers who also used a VMware ESX zero-day.
A critical Linux kernel flaw allows remote root attacks on servers using MPTCP (Multipath TCP).
The official Claude Code extension on the Cursor Marketplace was trojanized with a persistent SSH backdoor; WIRED reports it reached thousands of developer devices.
North Korea-linked hackers are blamed for the record $6.3 billion Binance theft, which Binance links to a compromised DevOps laptop; nearly $3 billion has been frozen.
Breaches: Florida says 4.9 million people had SSNs leaked from its financial aid site, and more than $2 million was drained from Polymarket traders via a third-party supply-chain attack.

actions: Apply Linux kernel fixes for CVE-2026-46300 today (KEV due 2026-10-31) and your distribution's fix for the MPTCP remote-root flaw.
Patch self-managed GitLab CE/EE for CVE-2026-97229 and Cisco ASA/FTD for CVE-2026-76418 before the 2026-11-01 KEV deadline.
Patch the two Ivanti Connect Secure flaws CISA added to KEV on 2026-10-30 (due 2026-11-02 and 2026-11-13).
Check Palo Alto firewalls for signs of the PHP2Shell chained compromise, and patch VMware ESX for CVE-2026-41709.
If developers use the Claude Code extension in Cursor, check it against the vendor advisory and look for unexpected SSH keys or services.
Patch Drupal Commerce for CVE-2026-118539 and Cisco SD-WAN for CVE-2026-20127, and hunt for KeyDrift malware.
